newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Boral plans to float gas business - paper.
newsitem.headline: Boral plans to float gas business - paper.

text.p: Diversified industrial group Boral Ltd plans to outline later on Monday a A$400 million float of its energy assets, The Sydney Morning Herald reported.

The newspaper said the float vehicle, known as Envestra Ltd, would be the spin-off vehicle for a slice of the company's A$1.5 billion in energy assets. It said Envestra would own and operate gas distribution businesses in South Australia, Queensland and the Northern Territory which service over 400,000 customers.

"The Herald understands that the float will seek to raise A$400 million from the public and institutional shareholders," the newspaper said. It said Boral shareholders would receive a priority entitlement to buy shares in the issue.

The Herald said Boral would retain a 20 percent stake in Envestra. The newspaper said Boral would have a high amount of debt, bringing the total proceeds to Boral from the sale to between A$800 million and A$900 million.
Boral shares closed at A$4.10 on Friday, down two cents.
